mainTopic: The minimum sizes and heights of buildings in a sale or building deal, the opinions on who said each line of the משנה, and the height of the היכל.
overview: The amud opens with a short ברייתא that finishes the earlier topic of selling aged wine: the wine must stay good until סוכות. A new משנה then sets the minimum size of a בית חתנות for a son or a בית אלמנות for a daughter. רבי עקיבא says 4 by 6 אמות, and רבי ישמעאל objects that this is only a cowshed. The משנה lists standard building sizes, says a building's height is half its length plus half its width, and mentions the היכל as support. The גמרא explains that the משנה ties each house to one child because a son-in-law should not live with his in-laws, and it brings support from בן סירא. It then asks who said the cowshed line and who said 'ראיה לדבר', and gives two opinions for each question. It defines a טרקלין and a קנתיר. It also brings the view of אחרים that a building's height matches its roof beams. The amud ends with רבי חנינא resolving two פסוקים about the היכל's height, and with a question whose answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Aged wine must keep its quality until סוכות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that sold aged wine must keep aging, meaning stay good, until the חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: the wine must keep aging until the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a short ברייתא that closes the earlier discussion about someone who sells aged wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the topic was a seller who promises aged wine. This ברייתא adds a time limit for the seller's responsibility: the wine has to hold its quality until the חג, which is סוכות. This line wraps up that topic before the new משנה begins.

keyTerms.meaning: continues to age, meaning it stays good as aged wine
the festival, which here means סוכות

steps.whatToRemember: A seller of aged wine is responsible for it staying good until סוכות.

phrases.english: It was taught:
And it continues to age until the festival.
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier case of someone who sold aged wine. It has to stay good until סוכות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the wine-sale sugya from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Aged wine sold must keep its quality until סוכות.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: a bridal or widow's house is at least 4 by 6 cubits
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה: when land is sold, or a builder is hired, for a בית חתנות or a בית אלמנות, רבי עקיבא says the building must be at least 4x6 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone sells a plot to his friend, or if a builder takes on a plot from his friend to build a bridal house for the owner's son or a widow's home for his daughter, he must build 4 אמות by 6. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It sets the minimum size of a home that someone agreed to provide for a son's marriage or for a widowed daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two cases. In the first, a seller sells land for this purpose. In the second, a builder is hired to build on the owner's land. Either way the deal assumes a minimum size, and רבי עקיבא sets that size at 4 by 6 אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: one who takes on a job, a contractor
a bridal house, a home for a newly married son
a widowhood home, for a daughter who became a widow
cubit, a measure of about an arm's length

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who sells a plot of land to his fellow,
and likewise one who receives a plot from his fellow
to make for him a bridal house for his son
or a widowhood home for his daughter –
he builds four cubits by six,
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, a בית חתנות or בית אלמנות must be at least 4x6 אמות.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: that size is only a cowshed
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל disagrees. He says 4x6 is the size of a cowshed, not a home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: That is a cowshed!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל argues with רבי עקיבא. He says a 4x6 building is too small to count as a home for people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's point is that 4x6 is the standard size of a barn for cattle. A house for a married son or a widowed daughter has to be bigger than that, so he rejects רבי עקיבא's measure.

keyTerms.meaning: a cowshed, a barn for cattle

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
This is a cowshed!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: רֶפֶת בָּקָר הִיא זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreement with רבי עקיבא's size.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A 4x6 building is a cowshed, so a home must be larger.

steps.title: The size of a cowshed
steps.stepSummary: Someone who wants to build a cowshed builds it 4x6 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who wants to make a cowshed builds four אמות by six.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now begins a list of standard building sizes. It starts with the cowshed that רבי ישמעאל just mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line explains why רבי ישמעאל compared רבי עקיבא's measure to a cowshed: 4x6 is exactly the standard cowshed size. It also opens the list of sizes for other kinds of buildings.

phrases.english: One who wants to make a cowshed –
builds four cubits by six.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the comparison רבי ישמעאל made and starts the list of sizes.

steps.title: Sizes of a small house, a large house, and a banquet hall
steps.stepSummary: Small house is 6x8, large house is 8x10, and a טרקלין is 10x10.
steps.simpleTranslation: A small house is six by eight. A large house is eight by ten. A banquet hall is ten by ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of the standard size for each type of building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These standard sizes tell us what a buyer gets when a deal names a type of building. If someone sold or agreed to build a "small house," the minimum is 6x8 אמות, and the same idea applies to the other types.

keyTerms.meaning: a banquet hall, a large reception room

phrases.english: A small house – six by eight,
a large one – eight by ten,
a banquet hall – ten by ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of sizes.

steps.title: How tall a building should be
steps.stepSummary: A building's height equals half its length plus half its width.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its height is like half its length and half its width.
steps.whatsHappening: After the floor sizes, the משנה gives a rule for the height of each of these buildings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To find the height, take half the length and add half the width. For example, a small house of 6x8 has a height of 3 + 4 = 7 אמות.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean two different possible heights. You add the two halves together to get one height.

phrases.english: Its height is like half its length
plus half its width.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the height rule to the floor sizes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Height = half the length + half the width.

steps.title: Proof from the Sanctuary building
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל supports the height rule from the shape of the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a proof for this: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it is like the building of the היכל.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings support for the height rule from the measurements of the היכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The היכל was 40 אמות long and 20 wide, and it was 30 high. Half of 40 is 20 and half of 20 is 10, and 20 + 10 = 30. That matches the rule from the previous step.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sanctuary, the main building of the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: Standard sizes: cowshed 4x6, small house 6x8, large house 8x10, טרקלין 10x10. Height is half the length plus half the width, just like the היכל.

phrases.english: A proof for the matter –
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Like the building of the Sanctuary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the height rule.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that height equals half the length plus half the width.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The measurements of the היכל: 40 by 20 אמות, 30 high.

steps.title: Why does the משנה split son and daughter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה links the bridal house only to the son and the widowhood home only to the daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why does the משנה say 'a bridal house for his son, and a widowhood home for his daughter'? It should say 'a bridal house for his son or daughter, and a widowhood home for his son or daughter'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by questioning the wording of the משנה. It suggests a broader wording that would cover both son and daughter in both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Either a son or a daughter could need a house for a wedding or after being widowed. So it seems odd that the משנה gives each child only one kind of house. The גמרא wants to know what this narrow wording is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: A house built for a newly married couple
A home for a child who was widowed and came back
Why do I need it to say this? (the wording seems unnecessary or too narrow)
Let it teach / it should have said

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Why do I need it to teach
'A bridal house for his son,
and a widowhood home for his daughter'?
Let it teach: 'A bridal house for his son or his daughter,
and a widowhood home for his son or his daughter'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the wording of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's wording that limits each house to one child
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both son and daughter can need either kind of house, so the narrow wording looks unnecessary

steps.title: A son-in-law should not live with his in-laws
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is teaching good manners in passing: a son-in-law does not normally live in his father-in-law's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us something in passing: it is not proper for a son-in-law to live in his father-in-law's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the wording is on purpose. It teaches that a married couple normally lives with the husband's family, not the wife's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a חתן should not move in with his חמיו, the bride's father would not build a בית חתנות. A daughter comes back to her father's area only when she is widowed, so she gets the בית אלמנות.

keyTerms.term: מִלְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us a side lesson in passing

phrases.aramaic: מִלְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן,
phrases.english: It teaches us a matter in passing,
that it is not the proper way for a son-in-law
to live in his father-in-law's house.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִלְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the wording
steps.terutzResolutionType: The wording is deliberate and teaches a lesson about proper behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The narrow wording seemed to leave something out
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording reflects the proper practice that a son-in-law does not live with his in-laws

steps.title: Support from בן סירא
steps.stepSummary: A list from ספר בן סירא ranks a son-in-law living with his in-laws as lower than bran.
steps.simpleTranslation: As written in the book of בן סירא: I weighed everything on a scale and found nothing lighter than bran. Lighter than bran is a son-in-law living in his father-in-law's house. Lighter than him is a guest who brings in another guest. Lighter than that guest is one who answers before he hears, as the פסוק says: 'He who answers before he listens, it is foolishness and shame for him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the idea in step 9. It quotes ספר בן סירא, which calls a חתן living with his in-laws a very lowly thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list goes from bad to worse: bran, a חתן living with his in-laws, a guest who invites another guest, and someone who answers before listening. The last item is backed by a פסוק in משלי. The point for our sugya is that living with one's in-laws is not respectable.

keyTerms.meaning: An ancient book of wise sayings
Bran, the leftover husks of grain, almost worthless
A guest who brings in another guest
One who answers before he hears the question

phrases.english: As it is written in the book of ben Sira:
I weighed everything on the pan of a scale,
and I found nothing lighter than bran;

phrases.aramaic: וְקַל מִסּוּבִּין – חָתָן הַדָּר בְּבֵית חָמִיו;
phrases.english: but lighter than bran is a son-in-law who lives in his father-in-law's house;
and lighter than a son-in-law is a guest who brings in a guest;

phrases.aramaic: וְקַל מֵאוֹרֵחַ – מֵשִׁיב דָּבָר בְּטֶרֶם יִשְׁמָע –
phrases.english: and lighter than a guest is one who answers a matter before he hears it,
as it is said: 'He who answers a matter before he hears,
it is foolishness and shame for him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 9
steps.raayaObject: That a son-in-law should not live in his father-in-law's house
steps.raayaSupportSource: ספר בן סירא, with a פסוק from משלי
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives the בית חתנות to the son because a חתן should not live with his in-laws; בן סירא calls that lower than bran.

steps.title: Who said the cowshed line?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks who said the line about building a cowshed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: This is a cowshed! One who wants to build etc. Who says the line about the cowshed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה from steps 3 and 4. It asks who said the line 'one who wants to build a cowshed builds it 4 by 6.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line right after רבי ישמעאל's words has no name attached. It could be רבי ישמעאל continuing, or רבי עקיבא answering him. The גמרא wants to know which one.

keyTerms.meaning: A cowshed, a barn for cattle
Short for 'etc.', meaning the rest of the quote
Who teaches it? Who said this line?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: רֶפֶת בָּקָר הִיא זוֹ!
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says: This is a cowshed!
One who wants to build, etc.
The cowshed line, who teaches it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: who said a line in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא said the line about building a cowshed

steps.title: Two opinions on who said it
steps.stepSummary: Some say רבי ישמעאל said the line, and some say רבי עקיבא said it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבי ישמעאל teaches it, and some say רבי עקיבא teaches it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two possible answers. The next two steps explain what each answer means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This only names the two choices. How the line fits each speaker is explained right after.

keyTerms.meaning: There is one who says (one opinion is)
He is the one who teaches it

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל קָתָנֵי לַהּ,
phrases.english: There is one who says Rabbi Yishmael teaches it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא קָתָנֵי לַהּ.
phrases.english: and there is one who says Rabbi Akiva teaches it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 with two views
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either רבי ישמעאל or רבי עקיבא said the cowshed line

steps.title: If רבי עקיבא said it
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers: even though 4x6 is cowshed size, people sometimes live in a home that small.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says רבי עקיבא teaches it explains: Even though it is the size of a cowshed, sometimes a person makes his home like a cowshed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first view. רבי עקיבא answers רבי ישמעאל and defends his 4x6 size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא admits that 4x6 is cowshed size. But since some people really do live in homes that small, a builder who made 4x6 has done his job.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what he is saying

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא קָתָנֵי לַהּ –
phrases.english: There is one who says Rabbi Akiva teaches it,
and this is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרֶפֶת בָּקָר הִיא,
phrases.english: Even though it is the size of a cowshed,

phrases.aramaic: פְּעָמִים שֶׁאָדָם עוֹשֶׂה דִּירָתוֹ כְּרֶפֶת בָּקָר.
phrases.english: there are times when a person makes his home like a cowshed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא קָתָנֵי לַהּ וְהָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first opinion from step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A 4x6 house is enough, since some people live in homes that small

steps.title: If רבי ישמעאל said it
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל is proving his point: 4x6 is what people build for cows, so a home must be bigger.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says רבי ישמעאל teaches it explains: For one who wants to build a cowshed builds it four אמות by six.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second view. The cowshed line is רבי ישמעאל backing up his own claim against רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל points out that 4x6 is the normal size for a cowshed. So it cannot be the right size for a home for a person, which must be larger.

keyTerms.meaning: Cubits, a measure of about an arm's length

steps.whatToRemember: The cowshed line is either רבי עקיבא saying 'people sometimes live that small,' or רבי ישמעאל saying 'that size is only for cows.'

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל קָתָנֵי לַהּ –
phrases.english: And there is one who says Rabbi Yishmael teaches it,
and this is what he is saying:
For one who wants to build a cowshed
builds it four cubits by six.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל קָתָנֵי לַהּ וְהָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second opinion from step 12, the other side of step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 4x6 is the normal size of a cowshed, so a home for people must be bigger

steps.title: What is a banquet hall?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's size for a טרקלין and explains what kind of room it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says a banquet hall is ten by ten. What is a banquet hall? A pavilion of roses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next size from the משנה, ten by ten for a טרקלין, and explains the unusual word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses a borrowed word, טרקלין, that a reader might not know. The גמרא translates it into a familiar picture: a fancy room where people gather, like a rose pavilion. No argument here, just a definition.

keyTerms.meaning: A banquet hall or reception room

phrases.english: A banquet hall is ten by ten.
What is a banquet hall?
A pavilion of roses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the argument about the four by six house to the next size listed in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טרקלין is a fancy reception room, and its standard size is ten by ten.

steps.title: A ברייתא adds the size of a קנתיר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a קנתיר is twelve by twelve, and the גמרא explains what a קנתיר is.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: a קנתיר is twelve by twelve. What is a קנתיר? A courtyard of a mansion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with one more room size that our משנה does not list, and explains the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lists sizes only up to the טרקלין. The ברייתא adds a bigger space, the קנתיר, at twelve by twelve. The גמרא then defines it as a fancy courtyard in a large house.

phrases.english: It was taught: and a kanteir
is twelve by twelve.
What is a kanteir?
A courtyard of a mansion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more size to the list from step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קנתיר, a mansion's courtyard, is twelve by twelve.

steps.title: The משנה's rule for building height
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a building's height is half its length plus half its width, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל mentions the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its height is half its length plus half its width. A proof of the matter: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, like the building of the היכל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last part of the משנה about how tall these rooms must be. This is the setup for the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The height comes from a set formula: add half the length and half the width. The words 'ראיה לדבר' then appear right next to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's mention of the היכל. It is unclear who is saying those words, and the גמרא asks about that next.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary building of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Its height is like half its length and half its width,
a proof of the matter:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
like the building of the Sanctuary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the next line of the משנה after the room sizes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A building's standard height equals half its length plus half its width.

steps.title: Who says 'proof of the matter'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who in the משנה says the words 'ראיה לדבר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Proof of the matter': who teaches it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose words 'ראיה לדבר' are: the תנא קמא's, or רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase sits between the תנא קמא's rule and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's name, so it could belong to either one. Which speaker it belongs to changes whether the היכל is a real proof or something that is being questioned.

phrases.english: "Proof of the matter": who teaches it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the משנה line quoted in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which speaker in the משנה says the words 'ראיה לדבר'.

steps.title: First answer: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל brings the היכל as proof
steps.stepSummary: One opinion says רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says 'ראיה לדבר' and proves the height rule from the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבן שמעון בן גמליאל teaches it, and this is what he means: where is the proof? רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: everything follows the building of the היכל.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer gives the words to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He is supporting the height rule by pointing to the היכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees with the height formula. He shows it is correct because the היכל, the model building, was built with these proportions. So everyone should build that way.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what he means

phrases.english: There is one who says

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל קָתָנֵי לַהּ –
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel teaches it,
and this is what he is saying:
From where is there a proof of the matter?
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
Everything is like the building of the Sanctuary.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says 'ראיה לדבר' and uses the היכל to support the height rule.

steps.title: Second answer: the תנא קמא brings the proof and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is surprised
steps.stepSummary: Another opinion says the תנא קמא brings a proof from the היכל, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל wonders how the היכל can prove anything about ordinary homes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say the תנא קמא teaches it, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is expressing surprise. He says to the תנא קמא: your proof is from where, from the היכל?! Does everyone build like the היכל?
steps.whatsHappening: The second answer gives 'ראיה לדבר' to the תנא קמא. Here רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is pushing back against using the היכל as a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, the תנא קמא tried to prove the height rule from the היכל. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל objects that the היכל was a special, holy building. Regular people do not build their homes to match it, so it cannot set the standard for ordinary houses.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed teacher in the משנה
Is that to say...? (introduces a surprised question)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of the משנה. In one, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל uses the היכל to support the height rule. In the other, the תנא קמא used the היכל, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rejects that proof because ordinary people do not build like the היכל.
steps.confusionAlert: The same words, כבנין היכל, mean opposite things in the two readings. In the first they are a proof. In the second they are a surprised question challenging that proof.

phrases.english: And there is one who says
the first tanna teaches it,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אַתְמוֹהֵי קָא מַתְמַהּ,
phrases.english: and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is expressing astonishment,
and this is what he is saying to him [to the first tanna]:
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording, and they tell us he is talking to the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: A proof from where?
From the building of the Sanctuary?!
Is that to say that everyone
builds like the building of the Sanctuary?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, opposite answer to the question in step 18, as an alternative to step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא says 'ראיה לדבר' and points to the היכל. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is surprised, because ordinary homes are not built like the היכל.

steps.title: Others say the height equals the beams
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes אחרים, who say a building's height should match the length of its roof beams.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא: אחרים say: its height is like the length of its beams.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a different way of measuring how tall a building must be. אחרים say the height should equal the length of the roof beams.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a formula: half the length plus half the width. אחרים give a simpler measure that ties the height to the beams that stretch across the roof. This new statement is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others', a name the גמרא uses for certain תנאים

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא: Others say:
phrases.notes: 'אחרים' is a name for certain תנאים, quoted together as 'Others'.

phrases.english: Its height is like its beams.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a different תנא's measure for the building height discussed in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אחרים, a building's height equals the length of its roof beams.

steps.title: Why not just say height equals width
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אחרים did not simply say the height equals the width.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them say: its height is like its width!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of אחרים. The beams go across the width, so why not just say 'height equals width'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beams stretch from wall to wall across the width, so their length seems to be the same as the width. Saying 'beams' instead of 'width' looks like a roundabout way to say the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him say (why not say instead)

phrases.english: And let him say: its height is like its width!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'כְּקוֹרוֹתָיו' in the words of אחרים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Beams run across the width, so 'like its beams' seems to mean 'like its width', and the simpler wording should have been used.

steps.title: First answer: the house is wider at the top
steps.stepSummary: The house is wider at the top, so the beams are longer than the floor's width.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: a house is wider at the top.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer. The walls get thinner as they go up, so the space at the top is wider than at the floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the top is wider, the beams up there are longer than the floor's width. So 'like its beams' gives a bigger number than 'like its width', and the wording is exact.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces one possible answer)

phrases.english: If you want, say: a house is wider at the top,
phrases.notes: The walls are thinner up high, so there is more room inside near the roof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the two measures are really different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Beam length and width are the same, so 'beams' is extra wording.
steps.terutzMaskana: The top of the house is wider than the floor, so the beams are longer than the width.

steps.title: Second answer: the beams sit in holes in the wall
steps.stepSummary: The ends of the beams go into holes in the walls, so the beams are longer than the inside width.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: because there are holes in the walls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the same question. The beams rest in holes in the walls, so they stretch past the inside width of the room.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the walls do not need to get thinner. Even in a room with straight walls, each beam is longer than the inside width because its ends sit inside the walls. So again 'beams' means a larger measure than 'width'.

keyTerms.meaning: Holes or niches in the wall

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
Because there are holes in the walls.
phrases.notes: These are the holes where the ends of the beams are set into the walls.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא בֵּי כַוֵּוי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, separate answer to the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Second way to show the two measures are different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Beam length equals the inside width.
steps.terutzMaskana: The beams reach into holes in the walls, so they are longer than the inside width.
steps.whatToRemember: אחרים say height equals the beams and not the width, because the beams are longer than the width. Either the house is wider at the top, or the beam ends sit in holes in the walls.

steps.title: Two verses disagree about the height of the היכל
steps.stepSummary: In the villages, people showed רבי חנינא two פסוקים: one says the house was thirty אמות high, the other says twenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא went out to the villages. They showed him two verses that seem to contradict each other. It is written: 'And the house that King שלמה built for ה׳ was sixty אמות long, twenty wide, and thirty אמות high.' And it is written: 'And before the דביר was twenty אמות long, twenty אמות wide, and twenty אמות high!'
steps.whatsHappening: Still on the topic of the height of the היכל, the גמרא tells a story. People in the villages showed רבי חנינא two פסוקים in מלכים that seem to give different heights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says the house שלמה built was thirty אמות tall. The second פסוק, about the inner part, says it was twenty tall. Both seem to describe the same height, so how can both be true?

keyTerms.meaning: They set verses against each other (pointed out a contradiction)
The inner room, the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina went out to the villages,
They set verses against each other before him:
phrases.notes: The village people showed him two פסוקים that seem to disagree.

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב: ״וְהַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר בָּנָה הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה לַה׳ –
phrases.english: It is written: "And the house that King Shlomo built for ה׳
sixty amos was its length, and twenty its width,
and thirty amos its height";
And it is written: "And before the inner room

phrases.aramaic: עֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה אֹרֶךְ, וְעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה רֹחַב,
phrases.english: twenty amos in length, and twenty amos in width,
and twenty amos its height"!
phrases.notes: מלכים א 6:20. The first פסוק said thirty, and this one says twenty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from building height in general to a contradiction about the height of the היכל, which was mentioned in steps 19-20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The heights of the היכל given in מלכים א 6:2 and 6:20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק says thirty אמות and the other says twenty, so they seem to contradict each other.

steps.title: The twenty is measured from the top of the כרובים
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא answers that the second פסוק counts only the space from the top of the כרובים upward.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: when it counts, it counts from the edge of the כרובים and up.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers the villagers. The פסוק that says twenty does not measure from the floor. It measures from the top of the כרובים upward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full height is thirty אמות, measured from the floor. The second פסוק leaves out the bottom part where the כרובים stood and counts only the twenty אמות above them. So there is no real contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: The top edge of the כרובים

phrases.english: He said to them: when it counts,
it counts from the edge of the כרובים and up.
phrases.notes: The כרובים were ten אמות tall (מלכים א 6:23), so ten plus twenty makes thirty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each פסוק measures from a different starting point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים measure the full height from the floor, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second פסוק counts only from the top of the כרובים upward; the full height is thirty.

steps.title: What does this teach us
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what lesson the פסוק teaches by counting only the space above the כרובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the פסוק wants to teach by measuring only above the כרובים. This line sets up the answer, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know the second פסוק skips the space where the כרובים stood, the גמרא wants to know why. Leaving out that space must be teaching something, and the גמרא explains what on the next amud.

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the answer given in step 26. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the פסוק teaches by measuring the height only from the top of the כרובים.
